kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source's six-row table.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the six TERM/DEFINITION/EXAMPLE rows; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three-question reading of the table (QUESTION 1 — IS THE STEM MAKING A MAGNITUDE CLAIM? Four rows compare the observed combination to THE SUM of the individual effects and print it as arithmetic: '2 + 2 < 4' antagonistic, '2 + 2 = 4' additive, '2 + 2 > 4' synergistic, '2 + 0 > 2' potentiation. QUESTION 2 — DOES THE PARTNER DO ANYTHING ALONE? the zero-partner case is potentiation by the source's own definition ('Similar to synergism, but drug B (with no therapeutic action alone) enhances the therapeutic action of drug A') — both partners active and beating the sum is synergism. QUESTION 3 — IS THE SECOND SUBSTANCE A DRUG AT ALL, OR THE SAME DRUG RE-DOSED? a falling response with a second drug is antagonistic (morphine with naloxone); the same drug re-dosed is tachyphylactic (oxymetazoline). The permissive row answers none of the three — it makes a REQUIREMENT claim ('Presence of substance A is required for the full effects of substance B'), which is why it carries no math metaphor) — KYP's synthesis of the six rows into one reading order (magnitude? → who acts alone? → one drug or two?).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the six rows as parallel table entries without a unified reading protocol; the sum-reference framing, the zero-partner test, and the count-the-drugs-then-check-the-clock rule are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP-original mnemonics (1 — READ THE SIGN, NAME THE TERM: < is Antagonistic (morphine with naloxone), = is Additive (aspirin and acetaminophen), > is Synergistic (clopidogrel with aspirin), 0> is Potentiation (carbidopa + levodopa). 2 — THE ZERO RULES POTENTIATION: a partner that is a ZERO alone and still beats the solitary drug is potentiation ('2 + 0 > 2'), not synergism ('2 + 2 > 4'). 3 — PERMISSIVE = PERMISSION, NOT POWER: cortisol does not add pressor force; it permits catecholamines their full effect. 4 — TACHYPHYLAXIS = THE DRUG TIRES OF ITSELF: same drug, repeat dosing, response falls — no partner, no sum). The Drug effect modifications section prints NO margin mnemonic — all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 234's Drug effect modifications section prints NO mnemonic; all four codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 256). The Drug effect modifications section is typeset text only — one six-row TERM/DEFINITION/EXAMPLE table in the PDF text layer. The table is carried verbatim (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION) in the note's table block and re-typeset in the registry visual (the sign ladder for the four math-metaphor rows, dedicated panels for the permissive and tachyphylactic rows, and the verbatim examples strip) — short attributed definition sentences and drug pairs, not artwork reproductions; no copyrighted artwork exists on this section of the page and nothing is reproduced. The section prints NO margin mnemonic; the KYP memory layer adds four original codes (READ THE SIGN, NAME THE TERM; THE ZERO RULES POTENTIATION; PERMISSIVE = PERMISSION, NOT POWER; TACHYPHYLAXIS = THE DRUG TIRES OF ITSELF). The clinical anchors that extend past the source page (adrenal-crisis pressor refractoriness for the permissive row; dual antiplatelet therapy and ED naloxone for the synergistic/antagonistic rows; rhinitis medicamentosa for the tachyphylactic row; and the tachyphylaxis-vs-tolerance time-course distinction) are flagged as KYP clinical anchors wherever they appear. No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. EXCLUSION: the 'Autonomic receptors' section occupies the LOWER portion of this SAME page — its second banner, its header, and the AUTONOMIC/SOMATIC overview diagram are the SEPARATE PENDING topic 'autonomic-receptors' and are EXCLUDED from this topic: PH10 pins the same source page (pdf 256 / book 234) for its UPPER portion only.
